### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e33a636ddff2704df84ebe65d59e11daee56a8b8` — the merge of head `bb3fbd6443ae9565f8925130fe64872e9b78d982` into base `9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e33a636ddff2704df84ebe65d59e11daee56a8b8 && git checkout e33a636ddff2704df84ebe65d59e11daee56a8b8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff bb3fbd6443ae9565f8925130fe64872e9b78d982 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff && git merge --no-ff bb3fbd6443ae9565f8925130fe64872e9b78d982

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

review#3 (area-lease pilot #33059, area E2).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb3fbd6443ae9565f8925130fe64872e9b78d982`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-revise.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-flow-name-per-namespace.dogfood.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/stored-process-package-backfill.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (read only)

### ① Derived judgments

- `requestFlowSlot`: a request stamped with a package is answered by that package's slot only. When that package holds no slot, the answer is `WithdrawnRequestFlow` naming the remaining holders, and it never falls through to the run's key or the bare read. Both of those could serve another package's flow, as the FROM table measures. Correct for ADR-0150 D8 R7.
- The stamp is only ever a package id. `process_package` is written from `flowSlot.packageId` when truthy (`approval-service.ts` ~L4946), and the backfill binds only `holder.kind === 'package'` answers (`stored-process-package-backfill.ts` L148–152). So an environment-authored flow's request (stamp null) never takes the withdrawn branch. Its path is unchanged.
- `requestFlow`: withdrawn + no holder → `null` (the bare read's deleted-flow answer, unchanged); withdrawn + holders → `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`not-held-by-qualifier`, stamped package as qualifier, every holder named, nothing read). `requestFlowKey` → `null` (the queue reads environment-wide). The request-open path asks no package and narrows the union away explicitly. One-holder and still-holding answers are pinned as CONTROLs (`[#31696]` stays green).
- nit N1: the refusal sentence says "install package X again". If the engine also drops a DISABLED package's slots (not only an uninstalled one's), the remedy is "install or re-enable". Make the sentence cover both, or confirm disable keeps the slot.
- The unit-harness observation (an engine run-key resume onto another package's graph) is the engine's, correctly left out of scope and noted.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch with `!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: every moved door now refuses or answers nothing where it served another package's flow. No export or schema change. `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs: none — REASON` hold.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Approval actions on records (send-back, resubmit) for requests whose package was uninstalled: fail-closed, nothing written.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area E2 session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw.
- CI at this head when read (16:12Z): 19 green, 14 running, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check.

### ④ Design judgment

A request belongs to the flow of the package it was opened on (D8 R7). Answering from another package's same-named flow showed approvers a graph that never ran the request and could act on it. Refusing with every holder named, and keeping the deleted-flow answer when no holder is left, is the minimal correct behaviour. The booted dogfood pin covers the real install, uninstall and reinstall path. Holds.
